name: Schierlitz ISD
aliases: TVT versus TOT in intrinsic sphincter deficiency
question: Does retropubic tension-free vaginal tape reduce persistent stress incontinence compared with transobturator tape in women with intrinsic sphincter deficiency?

design.population: Women with urodynamic stress urinary incontinence and intrinsic sphincter deficiency (maximum urethral closure pressure ≤20 cm H2O and/or leak-point pressure rise ≤60 cm H2O), with or without concomitant pelvic organ prolapse repair.
design.description: Randomized controlled trial at two Australian urogynecology centers
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 1254-1255; Results, p 1255

verdictNote: Urodynamic stress incontinence at six months was lower with retropubic TVT among women assessed.
takeaway: In women with urodynamic stress incontinence and intrinsic sphincter deficiency, retropubic TVT had less urodynamic stress incontinence at six months than Monarc transobturator tape (14/67 [21%] versus 32/71 [45%] assessed; P=.004).

reports.label: Six-month primary report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref, published-print date-parts: December 2008; PubMed citation

results.measure: Presence of urodynamic stress incontinence at 6 months among women assessed urodynamically
results.note: Available-case urodynamic analysis in 138/164 randomized women; 17 asymptomatic women declined repeat testing.
Observed repeat sling surgery among women assessed at six months; distinct from the imputed intention-to-treat request estimate.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3, p 1259; Results, p 1257

results.measure: Intention-to-treat estimate of request for repeat surgery at six months; withdrawals and losses counted as failures, asymptomatic non-testers as successes
results.note: RR compares transobturator with retropubic tape; rate difference 9.7 percentage points (95% CI 0–19.9). The paper misprints 13/82 as 19.9%.

harms.label: Intraoperative bladder and vaginal perforation
harms.note: One allocated TVT patient received Monarc after repeated bladder perforation; no urethral or bowel injury or transfusion in either arm.
harms.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 1258; Results, p 1255

harms.label: Groin infection requiring drainage and persistent obturator pain
harms.note: Abscess drained at six months with partial sling removal, antibiotics, and later pubovaginal sling.
harms.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 1258; Results, p 1257

delivery.label: Concomitant prolapse repair and catheter pathway
delivery.note: Sling-alone catheter was removed at operation end; concomitant repair often had catheter and vaginal pack for 24–48 hours.
delivery.locator: Full text, Table 1, p 1257; Methods, p 1255

delivery.label: Sling device and technique

values.ctl: American Medical Systems Monarc transobturator subfascial hammock

delivery.note: Surgeons had independently performed at least 15 of each procedure; both tapes were tensioned over fine scissors, with routine cystoscopy and preoperative antibiotic prophylaxis.

results.endpoint: Repeat surgery for stress urinary incontinence
results.measure: Symptomatic stress incontinence requiring repeat surgery during follow-up; one TVT event occurred at 43.7 months
results.note: HR compares transobturator with retropubic tape in time-to-event analysis. Intention-to-treat rate difference 17.1 percentage points (95% CI 8.4–25.8); transobturator median time to repeat surgery 15.6 months (IQR 11.8–41.4). The single TVT repeat operation was at 43.7 months.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 324; Table 1, p 324; Figure 2, p 325

results.note: Scores improved from baseline within both groups (P<.001), without a between-arm difference.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 325; Results, p 325

results.measure: IIQ-7 short form change from baseline to 36 months
results.note: Table 2 reports an unlabeled interval of 0.3–4.3 around the between-group difference; discussion describes greater improvement with transobturator tape. The table’s change scores and difference do not reconcile arithmetically.
